title: Occam's Razor for Big Data? On Detecting Quality in Large Unstructured Datasets
findings: The paper suggests that cultural and religious backgrounds significantly influence perceptions of AI. Western cultures, influenced by monotheistic religions like Christianity, may perceive the creation of artificial, human-like beings as 'sinful' or unsettling (drawing parallels to the story of Frankenstein), leading to feelings of unease towards humanoids. In contrast, Eastern cultures with polytheistic traditions, such as Japanese Shintoism, tend to be more accepting of artificial life and humanoid robots.
